# GridViewFocus: neo-focus-pointer survives blur on a loaded host

## Context

`test/playwright/e2e/grid/GridViewFocus.spec.mjs` is the whitebox witness for the grid's View-owned focus and its input-modality contract (#15195). Its blur arm fails intermittently: after `blur()`, the View still carries `neo-focus-pointer` when the 5 s poll expires.

```
Error: blur clears the pointer modality class
Expected: false
Received: true
Timeout 5000ms exceeded while waiting on the predicate
```

Observed while reviewing PR #20143 (Resolves #20142), which makes the six `lockedColumns` specs connect under a private `NEO_NL_PORT`. Every run below used `--workers=1`, `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` set to a Brain clone, a private `NEO_NL_PORT=18943`, and one macOS host carrying several live seats.

| Tree | Selection | Result | Wall time |
|---|---|---|---|
| PR head `fae4161a92` | the six `lockedColumns` specs | GridViewFocus failed, 2 of 2 runs | 45.6 s, 43.6 s |
| PR base `79dd27e972`, app config pointed at the private port* | the same six | failed 1 of 2 | 37.7 s (fail), 30.1 s (pass) |
| PR head | GridViewFocus alone, `--repeat-each=8` | 8 of 8 passed | — |
| PR head | `ColumnCrossBodyDnD` or `ColumnOverdragScroll` + GridViewFocus | 2 of 2 passed | 14–16 s |
| PR head | those two + GridViewFocus | 2 of 2 passed | 21–22 s |

\* `"neuralLinkUrl": "ws://127.0.0.1:18943"` was written into `examples/grid/lockedColumns/neo-config.json` for the run and reverted after it. On base, this lets the app reach the private Bridge without #20143's ordering change.

The PR author's six-spec run on another seat passed 10/10 in 29.4 s. Failing runs are the slow ones, and run order is identical in every batch (GridViewFocus runs 5th). So the observed trigger is load, not which spec runs before it. The failure exists on base, so #20143 did not introduce it.

Who sees it: any seat that runs the `lockedColumns` whitebox specs as a batch on a busy host. Once #20143 merges, that includes every seat running the NL battery on a private port. CI runs these specs in sharded jobs on the default port; whether its runners ever hit the timing is unknown.

## The Problem

The spec reads the pointer stamp without being able to tell whose stamp it is. That leaves its final `blur()` racing a focus request that is still in flight.

1. A row click in `bodyStart` focuses the View natively on mousedown. One worker round trip later, `grid.Body#onRowClick` → `view.focus(view.id, false, true, 'pointer')` → `Neo.main.DomAccess.focus` stamps `neo-focus-pointer` and calls `node.focus()`.
2. The spec then clicks a row in `body` and in `bodyEnd`. The View keeps focus across those clicks, so nothing clears the class. Each region's poll for `pointer === true` is satisfied at once by region 1's stamp, not by the region's own request (`GridViewFocus.spec.mjs`, the per-region loop).
3. The blur arm runs right after the `bodyEnd` poll: `document.getElementById(viewId).blur()`. If `bodyEnd`'s `DomAccess.focus` has not yet arrived, it lands after the blur, stamps the class again and focuses the View again. The class then survives the whole 5 s poll.

4. The keyboard arm has the same shape. It clicks `navRow`, waits only for `activeElement` (satisfied natively on mousedown) and presses ArrowDown at once. If that click's `DomAccess.focus` arrives after the keydown, it re-adds `neo-focus-pointer`, and *"the pointer modality class is cleared after the switch"* reads `true`.

A loaded host stretches the worker round trip, which matches the wall-time split above. This is the leading hypothesis. AC-1 is the measurement that confirms or refutes it.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/main/DomAccess.mjs` `focus()`: for `modality: 'pointer'` it adds `neo-focus-pointer`, registers a one-shot `blur` listener that clears it, then calls `node.focus()`. Each call stamps and focuses unconditionally unless `unlessFocusWithin` names a container that currently holds focus.
- `src/grid/Body.mjs` `onRowClick`: the only grid caller with a modality. It does not pass `unlessFocusWithin`.
- Design authority: `"both self-clear on blur"` (`DomAccess.focus`, inline comment above the pointer branch), together with the spec's own docblock: *"the class self-clears on blur or the first keydown"* and *"what this bounds is the ring — never the gap, and never a stale stamp"*. The loop in step 2 does read a stale stamp, so the spec breaks its own stated bound.
- The hazard class has a record: `DomAccess.focus`'s `unlessFocusWithin` JSDoc says *"A worker decides focus one round trip late, so a choice the user made in between, such as a picked list item, would otherwise be taken back."*

## Diagnosis (AC-1, recorded 2026-10-27)

The hypothesis holds. The instrument is a review-only event log on the View: a `MutationObserver` on its `class`, plus `focus`/`blur` listeners armed just before the blur arm. It ran inside the six-spec batch on a private `NEO_NL_PORT`.

| Tree | Condition | Log after the spec's `blur()` (ms from arming) | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| dev `d47905526b` | 3 batches | `blur` → `class ''` → **`focus` → `class neo-focus-pointer` 1–6 ms later**, all 3 | failed 1 of 3 |
| dev `d47905526b` | 500 ms wait before the blur, 3 runs | `blur` → `class ''`; the next `focus` is the keyboard arm's own click, about 35 ms later | passed 3 of 3 |
| fix head | 3 batches | `blur` → `class ''`; the next `focus` is the keyboard arm's own click, about 36 ms later | passed 3 of 3 |

- **The re-stamp is the last click's in-flight request, not a reaction to the blur.** It appears in every dev batch, and the 500 ms wait removes it.
- **Pass or fail is the first poll read's timing.** The re-stamp lands 1–6 ms after the blur. A first read inside that gap passes, and one after it fails for the full 5 s.
- **The keyboard arm** was not seen racing in these runs: its click's stamp landed about 15 ms after the native focus, before ArrowDown. The same shape applies under more load, so the fix waits for that stamp too.

## The Fix

Test-only, in `test/playwright/e2e/grid/GridViewFocus.spec.mjs`:

1. Make every region's stamp poll witness that region's own request. Clear the stamp between regions (blur the View and poll `pointer === false`) before the next row click, so a later region can never pass on an earlier stamp.
2. With step 1 in place, the `bodyEnd` poll guarantees its request has landed before the blur arm runs. No new wait or sleep is needed.
3. Before ArrowDown, wait for `navRow`'s own pointer stamp. The blur arm has just cleared the class, so that stamp can only be this click's.
4. Keep every existing assertion: per-region View ownership, no ring at either sampled point, the keyboard swap, blur cleanup and scroll stability.

If AC-1 refutes the hypothesis, rewrite The Fix in this body before any code moves.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC-1:** A deterministic repro on `dev` (CDP `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate`, or a delayed worker reply) fails the blur arm. Its trace shows a `DomAccess.focus` with `modality: 'pointer'` landing after the spec's `blur()`, or the hypothesis is recorded as refuted with the trace that refutes it.
- [x] **AC-2:** Under that repro, GridViewFocus fails on `dev` and passes at the fix head (same instrument on both trees).
- [x] **AC-3:** The six `lockedColumns` specs pass as one batch on a private `NEO_NL_PORT`, 5 consecutive runs at the fix head on a loaded host, with run wall times recorded.
- [x] **AC-4:** The spec docblock's *"never a stale stamp"* holds: no region's poll can be satisfied by an earlier region's stamp.

## Out of Scope

- Whether `grid.Body#onRowClick` should pass `unlessFocusWithin` so that a late worker focus never takes focus back from where the user moved it. That is a product question (hypothesis — needs V-B-A before implementation). File it only if AC-1's trace shows the re-focus, not just the re-stamp.
- The harness ordering in #20142 / PR #20143.

## Avoided Traps

- A longer poll timeout or a fixed sleep before the blur. Either one hides the in-flight request instead of ordering the test after it.
- Reading `document.activeElement` as proof that the request landed. The View is focused natively on mousedown, before any worker reply.
